## ^1-1362

```gloss
\gla    Tattha katamo samatho Yā cittassa ṭhiti…pe… sammāsamādhi ayaṃ vuccati samatho
\glb    --     --     --      -- --       --        --           --   --      --
\glc    --     --     --      -- --       --        --           --   --      --
\t      1352. What is unguardedness of the sense doors? Here, perceiving forms with the eye, sounds with the ear, odors with the nose, flavors with the tongue, tangible objects with the body, or mental objects with the mind, one grasps at their general appearance and details. Whereby, while the respective faculty dwells unguarded, evil unwholesome states of covetousness and displeasure might flow in; one does not practice for its restraint, does not protect that faculty, does not undertake restraint in that faculty. The unguardedness, non-protection, non-guarding, non-restraint of these six faculties—this is called unguardedness of the sense doors.
```

## ^1-1365

```gloss
\gla    Tattha katamaṃ paggāhanimittaṃ Yo cetasiko vīriyārambho…pe… sammāvāyāmo idaṃ vuccati paggāhanimittaṃ
\glb    --     --      --              -- --       --               --          --   --      --
\glc    --     --      --              -- --       --               --          --   --      --
\t      1355. What is moderation in food? Here, some person, with reflection, skillfully takes food—not for sport, not for intoxication, not for adornment, not for beautification, but solely for the maintenance and continuance of this body, for the cessation of discomfort, for the support of the holy life. "Thus I will end old feelings and not produce new feelings, and there will be sustenance for me, blamelessness, and comfortable living." That satisfaction, moderation, reflection in food—this is called moderation in food.
```

## ^1-1409

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā Uddhaccasahagato cittuppādo etthuppannaṃ mohaṃ ṭhapetvā ime dhammā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā Cattāro diṭṭhigatavippayuttā lobhasahagatacittuppādā dve domanassasahagatacittuppādā ime dhammā siyā dassanena pahātabbahetukā siyā bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā

\glc    --     --     --        --              --               --         --           --    --       --  --     --        --              --      --                   --                      --  --                          --  --     --   --        --              --   --        --
\t      1399. What phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application? Wholesome and unwholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; eleven resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; two resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; eleven functional consciousnesses; the first fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the first supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the initial application and sustained application arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by initial application and sustained application.
```

## ^1-1410

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā Vicikicchāsahagato moho uddhaccasahagato moho catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ rūpañca nibbānañca ime dhammā neva dassanena na bhāvanāya pahātabbahetukā
\glb    --     --     --   --        -- --        --              --                 --   --               --   --     --      --      --     --      --     --   --      --             --      --         --  --     --   --        -- --        --
\glc    --     --     --   --        -- --        --              --                 --   --               --   --     --      --      --     --      --     --   --      --             --      --         --  --     --   --        -- --        --
\t      1400. What phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only? The second fine-material jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the second supramundane jhána in the five-fold system, wholesome and resultant – excluding the sustained application arising therein – and initial application – these phenomena are without initial application but with sustained application only.
```

## ^1-1411

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā ācayagāmino Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ akusalaṃ ime dhammā ācayagāmino
\glb    --     --     --          --   --      --      --       --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --          --   --      --      --       --  --     --
\t      1401. What phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads, wholesome and resultant, and the second jhána in the five-fold system; and sustained application arising therein; and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena are without initial application and without sustained application. Sustained application co-arising with initial application should not be said to be accompanied by initial application and sustained application, nor only by sustained application, nor without initial application and without sustained application.
```

## ^1-1412

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā apacayagāmino Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā ime dhammā apacayagāmino
\glb    --     --     --            --      --    --           --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --            --      --    --           --  --     --
\t      1402. What phenomena are accompanied by rapture? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; five resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána dyads and triads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána dyads and triads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the rapture arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by rapture.
```

## ^1-1413

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino Catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ rūpañca nibbānañca ime dhammā nevācayagāmināpacayagāmino
\glb    --     --     --                         --     --      --     --   --      --             --      --         --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --                         --     --      --     --   --      --             --      --         --  --     --
\t      1403. What phenomena are accompanied by happiness? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by joy; four unwholesome consciousnesses; six resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; five functional consciousnesses; the fine-material jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the supramundane jhána triads and tetrads, wholesome and resultant – excluding the happiness arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by happiness.
```

## ^1-1414

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā sekkhā Cattāro maggā apariyāpannā heṭṭhimāni ca tīṇi sāmaññaphalāni ime dhammā sekkhā
\glb    --     --     --     --      --    --           --         -- --   --             --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --     --      --    --           --         -- --   --             --  --     --
\t      1404. What phenomena are accompanied by equanimity? Four wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses accompanied by equanimity; six unwholesome consciousnesses; ten resultant wholesome sense-sphere consciousnesses; six resultant unwholesome consciousnesses; six functional consciousnesses; the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the four immaterial jhána consciousnesses, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the fourth supramundane jhána, wholesome and resultant – excluding the equanimity arising therein – these phenomena are accompanied by equanimity. Rapture is not accompanied by rapture, is accompanied by happiness, is not accompanied by equanimity. Happiness is not accompanied by happiness, may be accompanied by rapture, is not accompanied by equanimity, and may not be said to be accompanied by rapture. The two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure, body-consciousness accompanied by pain, the feeling of equanimity, and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena should not be said to be accompanied by rapture, nor by happiness, nor by equanimity.
```

## ^1-1415

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā asekkhā Upariṭṭhimaṃ arahattaphalaṃ ime dhammā asekkhā
\glb    --     --     --      --           --             --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --      --           --             --  --     --
\t      1405. What phenomena are to be abandoned by insight? The four consciousnesses associated with wrong view, and the consciousness accompanied by doubt – these phenomena are to be abandoned by insight.
```

## ^1-1416

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā Tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ akusalaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ rūpañca nibbānañca ime dhammā nevasekkhanāsekkhā

\t      1406. What phenomena are to be abandoned by development? The consciousness accompanied by restlessness – these phenomena are to be abandoned by development. The four greed-rooted consciousnesses dissociated from wrong view, and the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure – these phenomena may be abandoned by insight or by development.
```

## ^1-1417

```gloss

\t      1407. What phenomena are to be abandoned neither by insight nor by development? Wholesome consciousnesses in the four planes; resultant consciousnesses in the four planes; functional indeterminate consciousnesses in the three planes; and matter and Nibbána – these phenomena are to be abandoned neither by insight nor by development.
```


## ^1-1419

```gloss

\t      1409. Which states have roots to be abandoned by development? The consciousness accompanied by restlessness, excluding the delusion arising therein – these states have roots to be abandoned by development. The four consciousnesses accompanied by greed, dissociated from wrong view, and the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure – these states may have roots to be abandoned by seeing, or may have roots to be abandoned by development.
```

## ^1-1432

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā atītārammaṇā Viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ ime dhammā atītārammaṇā
\glb    --     --     --           --                --                      --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --           --                --                      --  --     --
\t      1422. What dhammas have immeasurable objects? The four paths not included (in the realms), the four fruitions of recluseship – these dhammas have immeasurable objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge; all unwholesome (consciousness) – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, not immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects or as having exalted objects. From wholesome sense-sphere consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; from functional consciousness, the four consciousnesses associated with knowledge; the fourth rūpa-jhāna, both wholesome and functional; functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity – these dhammas may have limited objects, may have exalted objects, may have immeasurable objects, and may not be describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. The rūpa-jhānas of the triple and quadruple systems, wholesome, resultant, and functional; the resultant of the fourth jhāna; the base of infinite space; the base of nothingness – these dhammas are not describable as having limited objects, or as having exalted objects, or as having immeasurable objects. Matter and Nibbāna are without object.
```

## ^1-1438

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā Rūpāyatanaṃ ime dhammā sanidassanasappaṭighā
\glb    --     --     --                    --          --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --                    --          --  --     --
\t      1428. Which phenomena are indeterminate? The four consciousnesses accompanied by greed dissociated from wrong view, consciousness accompanied by doubt, consciousness accompanied by restlessness, wholesome (consciousness) in the three planes, resultant (consciousness) in the four planes, functional indeterminate (consciousness) in the three planes, matter, and Nibbāna – these phenomena are indeterminate.
```

## ^1-1439

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā Cakkhāyatanaṃ…pe… phoṭṭhabbāyatanaṃ ime dhammā anidassanasappaṭighā
\glb    --     --     --                   --                --                --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --                   --                --                --  --     --
\t      1429. Which phenomena are path-objects? The four wisdom-associated wholesome consciousnesses of the sense sphere, and the four wisdom-associated functional consciousnesses – these phenomena may be path-objects, are not path-causes; they may be path-dominant, or cannot be described as path-objects or path-dominant. The four Noble Paths are not path-objects, are path-causes; they may be path-dominant, or cannot be described as path-dominant. The fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional, and the functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity – these phenomena may be path-objects; are not path-causes, are not path-dominant; or cannot be described as path-objects. The four wisdom-dissociated wholesome consciousnesses of the sense sphere, all unwholesome (consciousness), all resultant (consciousness) of the sense sphere, the six functional consciousnesses, the three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the four immaterial (attainments), wholesome, resultant, and functional, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena cannot be described as path-objects, path-causes, or path-dominant. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.
```

## ^1-1440

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ akusalaṃ catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ yañca rūpaṃ anidassanaṃ appaṭighaṃ dhammāyatanapariyāpannaṃ nibbānañca ime dhammā anidassanaappaṭighā Tikaṃ

\glc    --     --     --                  --     --      --      --       --     --      --     --   --      --             --    --    --          --         --                       --         --  --     --                  --
\t      1430. Which phenomena are arisen? Resultant (consciousness) in the four planes and matter born of kamma – these phenomena may be arisen, may be arising; cannot be described as unarisen. Wholesome (consciousness) and unwholesome (consciousness) in the four planes, functional indeterminate (consciousness) in the three planes, and matter not born of kamma – these phenomena may be arisen, may be unarisen; cannot be described as arising. Nibbāna cannot be described as arisen, unarisen, or arising.
```

## ^1-1444

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā ahetukā Vicikicchāsahagato moho uddhaccasahagato moho dvepañcaviññāṇāni tisso ca manodhātuyo pañca ca ahetukamanoviññāṇadhātuyo rūpañca nibbānañca ime dhammā ahetukā
\glb    --     --     --      --                 --   --               --   --                --    -- --          --    -- --                        --      --         --  --     --
\glc    --     --     --      --                 --   --               --   --                --    -- --          --    -- --                        --      --         --  --     --
\t      1434. Which phenomena have present objects? The two sets of fivefold sense consciousnesses and the three mind-elements – these phenomena have present objects. The ten resultant consciousnesses of the sense sphere, the resultant mind-consciousness element accompanied by equanimity of the unwholesome, the functional rootless mind-consciousness element accompanied by joy – these phenomena may have past objects, may have future objects, may have present objects. Wholesome (consciousness) of the sense sphere, unwholesome (consciousness), the nine functional consciousnesses, the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional – these phenomena may have past objects, may have future objects, may have present objects; or cannot be described as having past, future, or present objects. The three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the base of infinite space, the base of nothingness, the four supramundane paths, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena cannot be described as having past, future, or present objects. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.
```

## ^1-1447

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca Yattha dve tayo hetū ekato uppajjanti ime dhammā hetū ceva sahetukā ca
\glb    --     --     --   --   --       -- --     --  --   --   --    --         --  --     --   --   --       --
\glc    --     --     --   --   --       -- --     --  --   --   --    --         --  --     --   --   --       --
\t      1437. Which phenomena have external objects? The three and fourfold fine-material jhānas, wholesome, resultant, and functional, the resultant of the fourth jhána, the base of infinite space, the four supramundane paths, and the four fruits of recluseship – these phenomena have external objects. Except matter, all wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate phenomena of the sense sphere, and the fourth fine-material jhána, wholesome and functional – these phenomena may have internal objects, may have external objects, may have internal and external objects. The base of nothingness cannot be described as having internal, external, or internal and external objects. Matter and Nibbāna are objectless.
```

## ^1-1451

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā na hetū sahetukā Catūsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ akusalaṃ kāmāvacarassa vipākato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā catūsu bhūmīsu vipāko kāmāvacarakiriyato ahetuke cittuppāde ṭhapetvā tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ etthuppanne hetū ṭhapetvā ime dhammā na hetū sahetukā
\glb    --     --     -- --   --       --     --      --      --       --            --       --      --         --       --     --      --     --                 --      --         --       --   --      --             --          --   --       --  --     -- --   --
\glc    --     --     -- --   --       --     --      --      --       --            --       --      --         --       --     --      --     --                 --      --         --       --   --      --             --          --   --       --  --     -- --   --
\t      1441. What are the phenomena that are roots? The three wholesome roots, the three unwholesome roots, the three indeterminate roots. Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, they arise in wholesome states in the four planes. Non-delusion is a wholesome root, it arises in wholesome states in the four planes, excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge in sensuous wholesome states. Greed arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Hatred arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. Delusion arises in all unwholesome states. Non-greed is a resultant root, non-hatred is a resultant root, they arise in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant. Non-delusion is a resultant root, it arises in resultant states in the four planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous resultant, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge. Non-greed is a functional root, non-hatred is a functional root, they arise in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional. Non-delusion is a functional root, it arises in functional states in the three planes, excluding the rootless consciousnesses of the sensuous functional, and excluding the four consciousnesses dissociated from knowledge – these phenomena are roots.
```

```gloss
\t      1465. What are the taints? The four taints: taint of sensual desire, taint of existence, taint of views, taint of ignorance. The taint of sensual desire arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The taint of existence arises in the four consciousnesses accompanied by greed dissociated from wrong view. The taint of views arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. The taint of ignorance arises in all unwholesome states. These states are taints.
```



## ^1-1487

```gloss
\gla    Katame dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā Uddhaccasahagato moho tīsu bhūmīsu kusalaṃ tīsu bhūmīsu vipāko tīsu bhūmīsu kiriyābyākataṃ sabbañca rūpaṃ ime dhammā saṃyojanavippayuttā saṃyojaniyā
\glb    --     --     --                  --          --               --   --   --      --      --   --      --     --   --      --             --       --    --  --     --                  --
\glc    --     --     --                  --          --               --   --   --      --      --   --      --     --   --      --             --       --    --  --     --                  --
\t      1477. Which phenomena are fetters? The ten fetters: sensual craving, ill-will, conceit, wrong view, doubt, adherence to rites and rituals, craving for existence, envy, avarice, ignorance. Sensual craving arises in the eight greed-rooted consciousnesses. Ill-will arises in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Conceit arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Wrong view arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Doubt arises in the doubt-rooted consciousness. Adherence to rites and rituals arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view. Craving for existence arises in the four greed-rooted consciousnesses disjoined from wrong view. Envy and avarice arise in the two hate-rooted consciousnesses. Ignorance arises in all unwholesome consciousnesses – these phenomena are fetters.
```



## ^1-1499

```gloss

\t      1489. Which dhammas are ties? There are four ties: covetousness bodily tie, ill-will bodily tie, attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie, and dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie. The covetousness bodily tie arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. The ill-will bodily tie arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. The attachment to rites and rituals bodily tie and the dogmatic adherence to 'this is the truth' bodily tie arise in the four consciousnesses conjoined with wrong view – these dhammas are ties.
```

## ^1-1513

```gloss

\t      1503. What are the phenomena that are hindrances? Six hindrances: sensual desire hindrance, ill will hindrance, sloth and torpor hindrance, restlessness and worry hindrance, skeptical doubt hindrance, ignorance hindrance. Sensual desire hindrance arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed; ill will hindrance arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure; sloth and torpor hindrance arises in prompted unwholesome states; restlessness hindrance arises in consciousnesses accompanied by restlessness; worry hindrance arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure; skeptical doubt hindrance arises in consciousnesses accompanied by skeptical doubt; ignorance hindrance arises in all unwholesome states. These phenomena are hindrances.
```

```gloss
\t      1510. Which dhammas are liable to be hindered but are not hindrances themselves? Excluding the hindrances, the remaining unwholesome states, wholesome consciousness in the three planes, resultant consciousness in the three planes, functional consciousness in the three planes, and all matter – these dhammas are liable to be hindered but are not hindrances themselves. Dhammas not liable to be hindered should not be said to be hindrances and also liable to be hindered, or liable to be hindered but not hindrances themselves.
```



Wrong view itself is not to be classified as associated with wrong view, nor as disassociated from wrong view.


## ^1-1575

```gloss
\glc    --     --     --     --   --          -- --   --     --     --   --          --
\t      1565. What are defilements? The ten bases of defilements: greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, doubt, sloth, restlessness, shamelessness, fearlessness of wrongdoing. Greed arises in the eight consciousnesses accompanied by greed. Hatred arises in the two consciousnesses accompanied by displeasure. Delusion arises in all unwholesome states. Conceit arises in the four consciousnesses accompanied by greed, dissociated from wrong view. Wrong view arises in the four consciousnesses associated with wrong view. Doubt arises in the consciousness accompanied by doubt. Sloth arises in prompted unwholesome states. Restlessness, shamelessness, and fearlessness of wrongdoing arise in all unwholesome states. These states are defilements.
```

